question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

He is habituated to using words spoken with an unusual amount of __venom __when it comes to his in-laws.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. **benevolence**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"venom"** means a feeling of extreme bitterness or hatred. It often refers to a harmful or malicious disposition. (जहर)

 
 
• **Example:** His words were filled with venom as he spoke against his enemies.
 
 
 
• **"Benevolence"** refers to a disposition to do good, an act of kindness or charity. It is the opposite of malice or ill-will. (भलाई)
 
 
• **Example:** Her benevolence was evident when she donated generously to the charity.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'venom'** is **'benevolence'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. **benevolence**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Satire** (व्यंग्य): The use of humor, irony, or ridicule to criticize or expose.

 
 
• **Example:** The play was a satire on the current political situation.
 
 
 
• **Ambiguousness** (अस्पष्टता): The quality of being open to more than one interpretation; inexactness.
 
 
• **Example:** The ambiguousness of his statement left everyone confused.
 
 
 
• **Irony** (विडंबना): The expression of one's meaning by using language that normally signifies the opposite, typically for humorous or emphatic effect.
 
 
• **Example:** It was an irony that the fire station burned down.
